correctness.rationale: Put L=log n and u_n=b_n+y/r_*. At a fixed height y, the exponential tail is sqrt(L)e^(-y)/(nK) times exp[-r''(t_j)z²/(2r_*)](1+o(1)) at t_j+z/sqrt(L), uniformly on compact y,z sets. The shifted lattice has mesh sqrt(L)/n; the quadratic lower bounds at the minima give summable Gaussian majorants and the positive rate gap on their complement gives o(1) total tail mass. The all-site tail sum tends to e^(-y) while the maximum site tail tends to zero, so the product of the CDFs converges to exp(-e^(-y)). At any compact height window the exponential densities are on their positive support for all sufficiently large n. In the exact winner density the all-other-sites product has the same limit uniformly in the removed index and the factor r(i/n)/r_* tends to one on compact rescaled valley windows. Integrating the resulting compact-window density yields the Gaussian mixture times the Gumbel density. The limiting density has total mass one; equivalently the union bound at y=-A and the Gaussian tail control exclude escaping marks. This gives joint weak convergence, including the single-valley case and nearest-minimum ties. No result outside the stated nondegenerate interior-minimum independent exponential setting is audited. The frozen verifier was inspected, not executed. An independent finite diagnostic, `python3 -I /workspace/checks/1.py`, integrates the exact finite-row valley winner densities on [-5,14] for the displayed two-valley example. First-valley masses were 0.6035764 and 0.6038021 at n=4000 and n=32000 versus limiting 0.6043561, with >0.999999 of height mass in the window; this is not a convergence or rate certificate.
